help: the reviewer's one act (#483): reads the PR and refuses anything not OPEN, a body with no 'aims to complete #N' to flip, a title that copies no aimed issue's title (#479), an aimed issue whose open blocker the body does not aim to complete (#482), or refuse-class drift in the standing report; relocates once onto the base only if it moved (the lifetime's one rebase - rsc/test/ conflicts are the syntactic class, taken wholesale and settled by the gate's own regeneration; any other conflict aborts back to review), resyncs a clean checkout that holds the branch and says so, then flips the body's phrasing to closes as the LAST edit before the squash - a refused squash restores the body as found, so a flipped-but-unmerged PR cannot exist - lands the squash pinned to the head every check saw (no message flags, so the body is assembled from the branch's commits and keeps their signatures), converges this checkout on the merge commit, sweeps what the merge orphaned via prune --apply, and the last word is one anchored verdict: forge merge: DONE naming the squash, or NOT DONE naming the halt

args.name: pr
args.help: the PR to merge: a number, a URL, or a branch

gh pr view: reads the PR's state, base and head before anything else, its body for the phrase to flip, and its title for the copy check
reads the merge commit after the squash, to converge this checkout on it
gh issue view: reads each aimed issue's title (#479): a title that copies none of them refuses the merge before any enacting step
gh api: reads each aimed issue's open blockers (#482): a body that leaves one unaimed refuses the merge before any enacting step
git fetch origin <base> <head>: reads both refs to judge whether the base moved
git push --force-with-lease: WRITES the relocated head back to the PR, leased against the sha the merge read - only when the base had moved (refused loudly under YOGA_NO_SEND)
gh pr edit --body-file: WRITES the flipped body as the last edit before the squash: every 'aims to complete #N' becomes 'closes #N' - and WRITES it back as found if the squash refuses (refused loudly under YOGA_NO_SEND)
gh pr merge --squash: WRITES the merge, pinned to the merge's own sha of the head every check saw - fetched or just pushed, never re-read from the eventually-consistent API (#488; refused loudly under YOGA_NO_SEND)
git push origin --delete: prune --apply, sweeping the server branches this merge and its siblings left (refused loudly under YOGA_NO_SEND)
git fetch origin: reads the squash back so the base can fast-forward
